label: Events
description: Waits for events and starts tasks. Run as one task named `events` per project, and one in Shared, whenever this workflow has at least one automation; it runs unattended and may only start tasks and post notices. An automation is a named state-level transition into an `"async": true` child naming a step state: `{ "name": "push_main", "when": "on_event('git.push', { branch: 'main' })", "to": "push_main", "inputs": { "event": ".event", "workflow": { "text": "feature/review" }, "inputs": { "$literal": { "issue": { "$binding": ".event.payload.commits[0].message" } } } } }` with the child `"push_main": { "state": "system/events/start", "async": true }`. A second step is that child's own `{ "when": "true", "to": "push_main_2" }` into `"push_main_2": { "state": "system/events/notify", "async": true, "inputs": { "event": ".children.push_main.output.event", "text": { "text": "…" } } }`. Shared's copy is `{ "$ref": "$SYSTEM/workflows/system/events", "transitions": [ … ], "children": { … } }`, both lists spelled out. A project's copy keeps Shared's automations: `{ "$ref": "$BASE/workflows/system/events", "transitions": [ …its own lines, { "$ref": "...filter($BASE/workflows/system/events.transitions, (t) => !['ignored'].includes(t.name))" } ], "children": { "$ref": "$BASE/workflows/system/events.children", …its own children } }`.
